newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico revises up Dec trade surplus to $343 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico revises up Dec trade surplus to $343 mln.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry on Thursday announced a revised December trade surplus of $343 million and a revised surplus for the full year 1996 of $6.415 billion.

It said in a statement the revisions compared with preliminary figures of $220 million in December and $6.292 billion for 1996. It said the December figures were bumped up by revisions on the export side, in agriculture, mining and manufacturing, and on the import side in auto-related goods.
Exports reached $8.449 billion in December and $95.948 billion in 1996, while imports in December were $8.106 billion, and $89.533 billion for the year.

Manufacturing exports in December totalled $6.956 billion, up 22.1 percent from the same month in 1995. Sales abroad of petroleum products were $1.129 billion in the month, a 51.7 percent rise over the same period. The ministry said the bulk of that increase was due to higher oil export prices, which averaged $21.66 per barrel in December, while volume was up 12.7 percent.
Agricultural exports were $321 million in December, up 7.3 percent over the same month the previous year.

Imports of intermediate goods grew 23.8 percent in December, compared with the year before, to $6.191 billion. Capital goods imports rose 51.8 percent to $1.189 billion. Conusmer goods purchased abroad were up 42.8 percent compared with December 1995, at $726 million.
